e: Identification assigns a scientific name. Common is not scientific.

Taxonomy is the study of classification. Classification groups organisms so we can name them and see relatedness. Taxonomy is the science of naming and classifying organisms. Mutation is different: a mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait.
Hierarchical classification has eight taxa. With domain included, there are eight main taxonomic ranks. Classification groups organisms so we can name them and see relatedness. Six is not eight.

q: Top three domains are Archaea, Bacteria, _____.
e: Top three domains are Archaea, Bacteria, Eukarya. Eukarya are organisms whose cells have a true nucleus. Archaea are prokaryotes, often living in extreme habitats, and are not bacteria. Fungi is not Eukarya.
Domains are subdivided into seven levels. Older schemes listed seven ranks; adding domain makes eight. Nine is not seven.
The lowest taxonomic level is Species. A species is a group of organisms that can breed to produce fertile offspring. Genus is not Species.

Cladistics compares DNA to find relatedness. DNA carries the genetic code in a double helix of nucleotides. Cladistics groups organisms by shared derived characters and common ancestry. RNA is different: rNA is the nucleic acid that helps turn DNA information into protein.

Dichotomous means divided into two parts. A dichotomous key splits identification into two contrasting choices at each step, from general to specific. Four is different: four major environment components together are called the ecosphere.

q: Keys divide groups into two categories _____.
e: Keys divide groups into two categories repeatedly. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek. Rarely is not repeatedly.

q: Keys progress from general to more _____ characteristics.
e: Keys progress from general to more specific characteristics. Enzymes are specific: each active site fits a limited set of substrates. Complex is not specific.

Thallophyta has no embryo formation. A true embryo is part of the higher-plant life cycle; thallophytes were defined without that. Thallophytes have a simple body with no true embryo in the classical scheme. Spore is different: ferns and mosses spread by spores, not by flowers.
Bryophyta has spores and gametes formation. Gametes are sex cells: sperm and eggs, produced by meiosis. Bryophytes are non-vascular plants such as mosses. Flowers is not gametes.

Pteridophyta are Spore -bearing with vascular system. Ferns and mosses spread by spores, not by flowers. Pteridophytes are vascular, seedless plants such as ferns. Seed is different: seed plants are gymnosperms and angiosperms.
Gymnospermae are non-flowering, Seed -bearing. Seed plants are gymnosperms and angiosperms. Gymnosperms have vascular tissue and seeds but do not make flowers. Cone is not Seed.
Angiospermae are Flowering plants. Flowering is the mark of angiosperms. Angiosperms are flowering plants that enclose seeds in fruits. Vascular-less is not Flowering.

q: Fish have fins and body covered with _____.
e: Fish have fins and body covered with scales. Scales without feathers point toward reptiles in simple keys. Fish typically use gills; aquatic turtles more often use lungs and accessory surfaces. Hair is different: hair or fur is a mammal feature in simple vertebrate keys.

q: Amphibians have body _____ covered with scales.
e: Amphibians have body not covered with scales. Scales without feathers point toward reptiles in simple keys. Partially is not not.

q: Reptiles have four limbs or _____ limbs.
e: Reptiles have four limbs or without limbs. Four major environment components together are called the ecosphere. Two is different: dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.
Birds are warm-blooded with Feathers. Feathers mark birds in a vertebrate key, not mammals. Scales is different: scales without feathers point toward reptiles in simple keys.
Mammals are warm-blooded with Hair. Hair or fur is a mammal feature in simple vertebrate keys. Feathers is different: feathers mark birds in a vertebrate key, not mammals.

q: Biologists use morphology and _____ as keys.
e: Biologists use morphology and anatomy as keys. Anatomy studies internal structure of organisms. Morphology is the study of structure and form of organisms. Ecology is different: ecology studies how organisms interact with one another and with the abiotic world.

q: Keys provide a simple way to _____ organisms.
e: Keys provide a simple way to classify organisms. Preserve is not classify.

q: Cold-blooded vertebrates include Fish, Amphibian and _____.
e: Cold-blooded vertebrates include Fish, Amphibian and Reptile. Reptiles are scaly, air-breathing vertebrates that usually use lungs. Amphibians can use skin, mouth lining, and lungs for gas exchange. Mammal is different: mammals are warm-blooded vertebrates with hair and milk.
